reuse.why: Replaces the five server-side midpoint copies with one shared getExpectedAmount, reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules, and keeps the existing getScheduledAmount by delegating to it; the API handler calls the older wrapper instead of the new helper.

duplication.why: All inline midpoint expressions are gone; what remains is two overlapping shared entry points (getScheduledAmount and getExpectedAmount) for the same rule.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and every server layer (app, forecast, budget template, preview, API) calls it.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field; three release notes and a now-stale 'furthest from zero' comment in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions are minor noise.

maintainability.why: One definition decides missing/range/approx/single; a maintainer must still know that getScheduledAmount needs the op to apply the approximate rule, which the client callers do not pass.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every server amount site calls getExpectedAmount (or getScheduledAmount, which delegates to it).

disguised_duplication.where: The copies were removed, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter that only api/schedules-get passes (client callers keep the old call), getExpectedAmount takes op for an isapprox branch; forecast-schedules passes _amountOp ?? conditions.amount?.op as its own fallback.
